_: SEC-5 justified exceptions for tools/secret-scan.mjs. Each entry is a (file, key) pair, never a whole file, because allowlisting a file pre-authorizes every secret a later edit pastes into it. 'why' is mandatory and is the review surface: an entry whose reason does not survive reading is an entry to delete, not to keep. An entry matching nothing fails the scan, so this list cannot silently outlive what it exempts.

allow.why: CI harness fixture, not a secret: the SA password of an ephemeral SQL Server service container on the runner-private network, alive for one job and reachable by nothing outside it. It cannot be generated per run, because a service container's env is resolved at workflow parse time and cannot read a value a step produced.

CI harness fixture, not a secret: it signs tokens for a localhost server that the same job starts and kills. Unlike the SA password this one COULD be generated per run in a step, and is left committed only so the harness value sits next to the assertions that use it. That is a preference, not a constraint, and it is the weakest entry in this list.

CI harness fixture, not a secret: the connection string embedding the same ephemeral SA password allowlisted above. It is a second copy of that value rather than an independent one, which CFG-1 would object to if either were a committed configuration value rather than a workflow-local literal.

Test harness fixture, not a secret: a symmetric signing key used only by the in-process architecture-test host, which serves no traffic and holds no data. It has to be a committed constant because the tests both mint and verify with it. Found by this mechanism's first run and never named in the findings register, which is why it is recorded as E-17 rather than quietly exempted here.
